question: There is no specific antidote or chelating agent for aluminium phosphide (Celphos) poisoning; management is entirely supportive, focusing on cardiovascular stabilisation and organ support.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is TRUE — and a critical trap. Aluminium phosphide has NO antidote. Do not confuse it with organophosphate (antidote: atropine + pralidoxime) or iron poisoning (antidote: desferrioxamine). Phosphine gas kills by irreversible mitochondrial cytochrome-c oxidase inhibition; supportive care is the only option.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct and critically important. Unlike most other poisons covered in this module, aluminium phosphide has NO antidote. Phosphine gas causes direct mitochondrial toxicity and myocardial failure. Management is purely supportive: treat shock, arrhythmias, and metabolic acidosis; MgSO4 has been trialled but not proven. Mortality remains 50–90% in severe cases.
